result.manual:
Optical table: 2400 x 1200 mm breadboard. Coordinates in mm: x along the long side (0..2400), z across (0..1200), height = height above the breadboard (y). Yaw angles are in degrees in the table plane, measured from +x toward +z.
Pump output port (amplifier, 800 nm, ~100 fs FWHM, 1 kHz): x=2250, z=294, height=120, beam travelling toward -x (yaw 180). Collimated, 0.5 mm 1/e^2 radius, horizontally polarised (in the table plane).
Probe output port (OPA, 1300 nm, ~60 fs FWHM): x=2250, z=935, height=158, beam travelling toward -x (yaw 180). Collimated, 0.8 mm radius. The OPA is pumped by the same amplifier; both ports are path-matched at the amplifier's split EXCEPT for the OPA's internal path (see manual 'opa').
Laser housings occupy x > 2250 around each port. Both shutters start CLOSED (use unblock). Any beam leaving the table is a laser-safety violation (logged).
Desk (computer, monitor, scope, stage controller) at x=-300, z=600, beside the x=0 end. You walk on a walkway 300 mm outside the table edge (tool responses give your position there as you_at, or 'desk') at 0.5 m/s, and can reach 0.6 m in from the table edge. measure_path is a tape measure along the beam: good to about +/-5 mm. Catalogue, datasheets, manuals, buying, camera, signal reads, motorised stage moves and scans happen at the desk; knobs, placement and the IR card happen at the part. knob(..., watch=true) also returns a camera frame if you are within 1.5 m of the desk.
Placing a part takes ~5 min and lands within ~1 mm of the requested position; yaw set by eye is good to ~0.5 deg. Kinematic knobs then fine-tune (+/-50 mrad).
Already on the table, free: a sample mount with f = 100 mm achromatic lens and a flip-in camera at the lens focal plane (also images the lens plane), a 1 GHz oscilloscope at the desk, an IR viewer card, and beam-block shutters at both output ports.

OPA user manual (excerpt). Output: signal 1300 nm, ~60 fs, horizontally polarised (in the table plane, same as the 800 nm pump). The pump light travels an internal path inside the OPA before the output port. Calibrated internal optical path for this unit (serial on the housing): 1527 mm, relative to the amplifier output. To reach temporal overlap with the direct 800 nm beam, the 800 nm arm must be longer than the 1300 nm arm's table path by this amount. It cannot be measured from outside the housing.

Delay stage manual. place(stage, x, z, height, yaw): (x, z, height) is the stage reference point at the front of the rail; yaw is the direction light travels INTO the retroreflector (along the rail). The retroreflector apex sits 90 mm + stage position along the rail from the reference point; its entrance face is 40 mm in front of the apex, clear aperture radius 19.1 mm. A hollow retroreflector returns the beam exactly antiparallel, displaced through the apex: a beam entering d mm to one side of the apex line leaves d mm on the other side (2d separation). Enter about 10-15 mm off the apex so the return can be picked off by a mirror. Path added = 2 x (distance from entrance to apex). If the incoming beam is not parallel to the rail, the returned beam shifts sideways by about 2 x (stage travel) x (misalignment angle) as the stage moves; align the input beam parallel to the rail by checking the return at both ends of travel. Positions are in mm from 0 to the travel limit.

Sample mount with f = 100 mm lens. place(sample, x, z, height, yaw): (x, z, height) is the lens centre, yaw the direction light travels through the lens. The sample (and the installed diagnostic) sits at the focal plane 100 mm behind the lens. Lens clear aperture radius 12.7 mm (clipping from ~10.5 mm). A collimated beam hitting the lens at angle theta to its axis focuses at f x theta from the axis, whatever point of the lens it hits, so overlapping the foci means matching the beams' ANGLES; where they hit the lens sets their crossing angle and must stay inside the aperture. Focal spot radius ~50 um for both beams. install(item) swaps the diagnostic; it does not change any path. Flip-in camera: view_camera('sample') images the focal plane (5.5 um pixels, field of view +/-2.5 mm, sub-pixel centroids); view_camera('lens') shows where each beam hits the lens (mm). Each spot also reports relative_power: the fraction of that beam's output power reaching the sample (~2% reading noise), so clipping on an optic shows up as a dim spot. Camera image axes: h = horizontal, positive toward the direction (lens yaw - 90 deg) in the table plane; v = up. The lens axis is h = v = 0.
